title: Advocating with Purpose: Stacie Cavallaro on Building Bridges Between Industry and Community
summary: Read about the lessons Stacie has learned from the skeletal dysplasia community and why connection remains a core tenet of her approach.
body_markdown:
For Stacie Cavallaro, science has always sparked curiosity. That interest first ignited like a Bunsen burner, thanks to a “quirky and fun” high school chemistry teacher, whose enthusiasm made science feel “dynamic, human and full of possibility.”


But after college, her first role in a genomics lab left her wanting more human connection in her daily work.


That led her to healthcare marketing, where she discovered her knack for translating complex information into language people can understand and use. Today, Stacie leads BioMarin’s advocacy work for skeletal conditions – helping the company listen to communities, learn from their experiences and consider their perspectives when making decisions.


Stacie recently shared her reflections for our employee profile series, “The DNA of BioMarin,” which draws inspiration from the four bases of DNA: **A** (adenine), **T** (thymine), **C** (cytosine) and **G** (guanine) – by asking employees to explore the role of **A** spiration, **C** onnection, **T** ranslation and **G** ratitude in their work.


Read more about Stacie, Senior Director, Patient Advocacy Skeletal Conditions, the lessons she’s learned from the skeletal dysplasia community and why connection remains a core tenet of her approach.
